subject: storytime
title: The Tale of Benjamin Bunny
about: Beatrix Potter's 1904 sequel to Peter Rabbit: Peter's cousin Benjamin takes him back to Mr. McGregor's garden to get his jacket and shoes off the scarecrow, and old Mr. Benjamin Bunny shoos away the cat that keeps them stuck under a basket. This is a gentle retelling in first-grade words where nobody is hurt, and it keeps Potter's trit-trot of the pony; the book itself is in the public domain, so he can meet the real one at the library afterwards. Five pages long.
tip: Ask: what did Benjamin put in the red hanky, and who was it for?

book.author: Beatrix Potter (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: Peter and his cousin go back for his jacket and shoes.

passage.text:
One morning, a little rabbit sat on a grassy bank.
His name was Benjamin Bunny.
Trit-trot, trit-trot!
A pony and cart went down the road.
Mr. and Mrs. McGregor sat in the cart.
"They are going out for the day!" said Benjamin.
He hopped off to find his cousin Peter.
***
Peter sat all alone.
He had lost his jacket and shoes.
So he was wrapped up in a red hanky.
"Mr. McGregor put my things on his scarecrow," said Peter.
"Let's go get them back!" said Benjamin.
So they hopped to the garden wall.
They climbed down a pear tree into the garden.
***
There was the scarecrow!
It had on Peter's blue jacket and his shoes.
Peter put them on.
The shoes were full of rain.
Squish, squish!
Then Benjamin filled the red hanky with onions.
"A gift for your mother," he said.
Peter was worried.
He kept hearing noises.
***
The two bunnies came around a corner.
They stopped.
There sat a big cat!
They ran and hid under a big basket.
The cat came over and sat on top of it!
She sat there for five long hours.
Peter and Benjamin did not make a peep.
***
Then old Mr. Benjamin Bunny came along the wall.
He was Benjamin's father.
He saw the cat on the basket.
"Shoo, cat, shoo!" he said.
The cat ran far away.
He lifted the basket.
Out hopped Peter and Benjamin.
Then he took them home.
Peter gave the onions to his mother.
She was glad to have his jacket and shoes back.

cards.note: Benjamin's father came looking for his son and sent the cat running.
Peter lost them in The Tale of Peter Rabbit, and Mr. McGregor dressed his scarecrow in them.

cards.q: What did Benjamin put in the red hanky?
cards.note: A gift for Peter's mother; a hanky is a small square of cloth, like a napkin.

cards.q: Where did the bunnies hide from the cat?
cards.note: Then the cat sat on top of the basket for five long hours.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: Trit-trot, trit-trot: with the McGregors gone for the day, the bunnies dare to visit the garden.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: Old Mr. Benjamin Bunny took them home, and Peter gave his mother the onions.

cards.q: How did Peter feel in the garden?
cards.note: He kept hearing noises; after his last visit to that garden, who could blame him?

cards.q: Where does most of this story happen?
cards.note: The setting is where a story happens; this is the same garden as in Peter Rabbit.

cards.q: In the story, what does a 'scarecrow' do?
cards.note: Scare plus crow: a pretend person in old clothes that keeps birds off the plants.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
